video_caption: The video segment opens with a static screen resembling a digital whiteboard, featuring a physics problem diagram and explanatory text. A dashed line forms a continuous wave-like or serpentine path across the magnetic field. On the left portion of this diagram, a straight line segment, labeled 'l', is shown at an angle 'θ' relative to a horizontal dashed line, appearing to be tangent to the curved path at its lowest point. On the right side of the curved path, a vertical double-headed arrow indicates a height 'h' from the horizontal dashed line to the peak of the curve. The top of the screen shows various digital whiteboard tools, such as "Stylus," "Color," "Line," "Eraser," "Backgrounds," "Undo," "Redo," "Pages," "Previous," "Next," and "Erase." A voice welcomes viewers back to the Physics Sir JEE channel, mentioning the Path Finder Solutions Series and that this is Magnetism Check Your Understanding Problem Number 6.

A dashed line illustrates a cycloidal trajectory starting from the base of the slope, reaching a maximum vertical height 'h' relative to the horizontal line, and then continuing. At the 0:23 mark, the screen briefly flashes and then transitions to show a detailed problem statement above the diagram. The problem statement, labeled "6.", describes: "A charge particle starts sliding down a frictionless slope of inclination θ in presence of a horizontal uniform and static magnetic field of induction B directed perpendicularly into the plane of the figure and uniform gravitational field of the earth. Intensity of the gravitational field is g. After sliding an unknown distance l, the particle leaves the slope and follows a cycloidal trajectory as shown in the figure. If on the cycloid maximum vertical displacement of the particle is h, find the distance l it had slid on the slope." The diagram remains the same, with the magnetic field symbols ('X's) clearly visible across the entire field. The branding on the left ("PHYSICS SIR JEE™" and "PATH FINDER SOLUTIONS SERIES") also persists in this updated view.

The video segment displays a digital screen with a physics problem. At the top, a long text question (labeled "6.") reads: "A charge particle starts sliding down a frictionless slope of inclination $\theta$ in presence of a horizontal uniform and static magnetic field of induction $B$ directed perpendicularly into the plane of the figure and uniform gravitational field of the earth. Intensity of the gravitational field is $g$. After sliding an unknown distance $l$, the particle leaves the slope and follows a cycloidal trajectory as shown in the figure. If on the trajectory maximum vertical displacement of the particle is $h$, find the distance $l$ it had slid on the slope." Below the text, on the right side, there is a diagram illustrating the problem. The diagram shows an inclined plane at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. A particle slides down this slope for a distance labeled 'l'. The area around the slope and the subsequent trajectory is filled with 'X' symbols, indicating a magnetic field 'B' directed into the page. After leaving the slope, the particle follows a cycloidal path, depicted by a dashed line, with its maximum vertical displacement from the point where it left the slope indicated as 'h'. On the bottom left of the screen, there's a blue and black banner with the text "PHYSICS SIR JEE™" at the top and "PATHFINDER SOLUTIONS SERIES" below it. The overall screen shows elements of a digital whiteboard or presentation software, with icons for tools like stylus, color, eraser, and navigation at the top.

The video segment displays a screen recording of an educational resource. On the left side, a blue and white banner is visible with the text "PHYSICS SIR JEE™" at the top, and "PATHFINDER SOLUTIONS SERIES" in white text against a blue background below it. On the right, a physics problem is presented, featuring both text and a diagram. The diagram illustrates a charged particle sliding down an inclined plane of inclination θ (theta), traveling a distance *l*, and then following a cycloidal trajectory, reaching a maximum vertical displacement *h*. Throughout this segment, a cursor moves across the problem text, highlighting phrases like "leaves the slope" and "maximum vertical displacement". The background of the problem text is white, and the diagram is set against a grid with 'x' marks representing a uniform magnetic field B directed perpendicularly into the plane.

The video opens with a digital whiteboard displaying a menu bar at the top with options like "Status," "Color," and "Next." The main screen is divided into two sections. On the left, a smaller image of a previous slide is shown, titled "ALL METHODS DISCUSSED" in green and yellow text. This image contains text like "PROTON SLIPS TO FALL UNDER GRAVITY," "MAGNETIC FIELD SAVES IT," "A BONUS TRICK OF FIELD TRANSFORMATIONS FOR OLYMPIAD ASPIRANTS," "A LENGTHY PROBLEM SOLVED USING 'ROLLING DISC' ANALOGUE," and "A MUST SEE MULTI-CONCEPTUAL PHYSICS CHALLENGE," along with emojis of a winking face and a wizard. It also displays "PHYSICS SIR JEE™" and a small physics diagram. Below this image, bold red text reads "LINK IS IN THE DESCRIPTION BELOW OR i BUTTON ABOVE." On the right side of the screen, blue and yellow text states "ROLLING DISC ANALOGY AND FIELD TRANSFORMATION TECHNIQUE." A male voice is heard discussing a "transformation technique" that is "least discussed" and will provide "answer much more quicker," also mentioning to "watch this video." At 0:12, the screen abruptly transitions to a new slide with a black background. The new slide features an orange title at the top: "STAGE 1: LOOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE" (English: STAGE 1: LOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE). Below this, a physics diagram illustrates an inclined plane with an angle θ, a red dot on the incline, and arrows indicating the magnetic field 'B' (pointing into the screen), gravity 'g' (downwards), and velocity 'u' (along the incline), along with a length 'l'. To the right of the diagram, handwritten equations appear: "N = 0 ⇒ mg cosθ = qBu ⇒ u = mg cosθ / qB" (English: Normal force = 0 implies mg cos theta = qBu implies u = mg cos theta divided by qB). Further down, the text "Using Work-energy theorem, (knowing that WB = 0)" (English: Using Work-energy theorem, (knowing that Work due to Magnetic field = 0)) is written, followed by the equations "mgl sinθ = 1/2 mu²" (English: mgl sin theta = one-half mu squared) and "u² = 2gl sinθ" (English: u squared = 2gl sin theta).

The screen displays a physics lecture slide on a black background, titled in orange text "STAGE 1 : LOOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE" (English: STAGE 1 : LOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE). A diagram in the center depicts a blue inclined plane with an angle θ, on which a small red particle is shown. A white line outlines the path along the incline, with an arrow labeled 'l' indicating the distance slid and a yellow arrow labeled 'u' for velocity. A downward green arrow labeled 'g' represents gravity, and a green circle with an 'X' and 'B' indicates a magnetic field pointing into the page. To the right, equations explain the condition for losing contact: "N = 0 ⇒ mg cosθ = qBu", which simplifies to a green-boxed formula "u = mg cosθ / qB". Below the diagram, additional text states "Using Wd-energy theorem, (knowing that W_g=0)" (English: Using Work-energy theorem, (knowing that Work_gravity=0)), followed by the equation "mgLsinθ = ½ mu²", and concluding with another green-boxed result "u² = 2gLsinθ".

The video segment displays a digital whiteboard with a black background, focused on a physics problem titled "STAGE 1 : LOOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE" (misspelling "LOOSING" for "LOSING"). On the left, a diagram illustrates an inclined plane set at an angle θ (theta) with the horizontal. A small red dot, representing an object, is shown at the top of the incline, and a length 'l' is marked along the incline. Arrows indicate the direction of gravity 'g' (downwards) and velocity 'u' (down the incline). A magnetic field 'B' is depicted as going into the screen (represented by a circle with an 'X' inside). To the right of the diagram, a box contains two equations: "N = 0 ⇒ mgcosθ = qBu" (meaning: Normal force is zero implies mass times gravity times cosine of theta equals charge times magnetic field times velocity) and "⇒ u = (mgcosθ) / (qB)" (meaning: This implies velocity u equals mass times gravity times cosine of theta divided by charge times magnetic field). Below the diagram, more text reads "Using WdK - energy theorem, (knowing that Ws = 0)" (meaning: Using the Work-energy theorem, knowing that the work done by spring is zero), followed by the equation "mglsinθ = (1/2)mu²" (meaning: Mass times gravity times length times sine of theta equals one-half mass times velocity squared). A final result is enclosed in a box: "u² = 2glsinθ" (meaning: Velocity squared equals two times gravity times length times sine of theta). The presenter's hand briefly appears in the lower right, pointing at the "Ws = 0" part of the text, emphasizing the lack of spring work.

The video displays a digital whiteboard with a black background, featuring handwritten text and diagrams in various colors, outlining "STAGE 2: MOTION IN CROSSED FIELDS". The screen is vertically split into two sections: "W.R.T GROUND FRAME" on the left and "W.R.T FRAME MOVING RIGHTWARDS" on the right. The left section shows a diagram of a particle, initially a block 'A' on an inclined plane (angle θ, length l), transitioning into a cycloidal path within a region of magnetic field 'B' (indicated by 'x' and dot symbols for into/out of the page), with a height 'h' marked. The right section presents a simplified diagram of a particle (green circle) between two horizontal dashed lines separated by '2R', with an upward force "qE" (orange text) and a downward force "mg" (red text) balancing each other, and a magnetic field symbol ('x' for into the page). Below both diagrams, in white, orange, and green text, are equations and explanations: "As E₀ = 0, the transformed E = Ū₀ × B, where Ū₀ is chosen Such that it cancels mg. In this frame, Particle executes Circular motion. So qE = mg ⇒ qŪ₀B = mg ⇒ Ū₀ = [mg / qB] Also R = [mU_rel / qB]". Throughout the segment, a digital pen highlights different parts of the diagrams and text, first tracing the cycloidal path on the left, then emphasizing the force vectors 'mg' and 'qE' on the right, and subsequently highlighting parts of the equations, specifically "E₀ = 0", "E = Ū₀ × B", "Ū₀", and finally "mg" and "qE" again to explain how the gravitational field is cancelled.

The video displays a static screen with a split view on a black background, titled "STAGE 2: MOTION IN CROSSED FIELDS" in white text. The left section, labeled "W.R.T GROUND FRAME," shows a diagram of a particle (labeled "A") on an inclined plane with length 'l' and angle 'theta,' then moving in a wavy, parabolic path within a uniform magnetic field (represented by dots). The maximum height of this path is labeled 'h.' The right section, labeled "W.R.T FRAME MOVING RIGHTWARDS," depicts a charged particle moving in a circular path with a vertical diameter labeled "2R" within a magnetic field (dots). Arrows indicate an upward velocity "v_E" and a downward gravitational force "mg." Below these diagrams, white text explains concepts: "As E_0 = 0, the transformed E = V_0 x B, where V_0 is chosen Such that it cancels mg. In this frame, Particle executes Circular motion." This is followed by a derivation leading to "V_0 = mg/qB" highlighted in a yellow box. Another formula, "R = mU_rel/qB," is also presented. Throughout the segment, a white cursor in the shape of a hand points to various elements of the diagrams and text, highlighting relevant parts of the explanation.

The video segment displays a series of educational slides with physics equations and diagrams on a black background. The first slide (00:03-00:06) is titled "STAGE 1: LOOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE" (meaning "LOSING CONTACT WITH INCLINE") and shows an inclined plane, a block, gravitational force 'g', and velocity 'u'. Equations for normal force, velocity 'u' in terms of 'mg cosθ / qVB', and 'u^2 = 2gl sinθ' from the work-energy theorem are presented in white text. A transition occurs at 00:06 to a slide titled "STAGE 2: MOTION IN CROSSED FIELDS," divided into "W.R.T GROUND FRAME" and "W.R.T FRAME MOVING RIGHTWARDS," illustrating particle trajectories (wave-like and circular) in magnetic (indicated by 'x' for into page and dots for out of page) and electric fields, with velocity 'VE' and 'mg' vectors. At 00:07, the scene transitions to a slide titled "MANIPULATING R," featuring three numbered white boxes: "1: We got, u = mg / qVB cosθ", "2: u^2 = 2gl sinθ", and "3: v₀ = mg / qVB". A vector diagram depicts initial velocity 'u' at an angle 'θ' to the horizontal, a rightward velocity 'v₀', and the resultant relative velocity 'u_net'. Throughout the segment, a red circle highlights key terms and equations as the narrator explains their origin and manipulation, for instance, highlighting 'mg/qVB' in boxes 1 and 3 to show a common factor. Arrows are drawn to connect equations and components, such as 'u = v₀ cosθ' and 'u_net = v₀ sinθ', showing vector decomposition. Further equations like `R^2 = m / (q^2 B^2) (v₀ sinθ)^2` and `h^2 / 4 = v₀^4 sin^2θ / g^2` are shown, leading to a final result `l = h / 4 tan^2θ` enclosed in a yellow box, derived by squaring and eliminating `v₀` using equation 3.

The video segment opens with a dark digital whiteboard displaying a complex physics derivation titled "MANIPULATING R" in yellow at the top. The board shows three green-outlined boxes at the top with equations: "u = mg/qB cosθ", "u² = 2gl sinθ", and "v₀ = mg/qB". Below these, a series of white handwritten equations connected by arrows illustrate a step-by-step manipulation, including "u = v₀ cosθ", "uᵣₑₗ = v₀ sinθ", and "R² = m²(v₀ sinθ)² / q²B²". A small vector diagram on the left depicts vectors labeled "u", "uᵣₑₗ", and "v₀", with an angle θ. The text further explains "Squaring and eliminating v₀" leading to "h²/4 = v₀⁴ sin²θ / g² (using eqn 3)", and finally, a yellow-outlined box with the result "l = h/4 tan²θ". A stylus cursor highlights these equations as the speaker explains them.

At 00:15, the screen transitions to another dark digital whiteboard titled "STAGE 2 : MOTION IN CROSSED FIELDS" in yellow. The slide is divided into two sections: "W.R.T GROUND FRAME" on the left and "W.R.T FRAME MOVING RIGHTWARDS" on the right, both in green. The left section shows a diagram of an inclined plane with a line 'l' and angle θ, and a wavy trajectory of a particle in a magnetic field (represented by 'X' symbols). A height 'h' is indicated. The right section shows a horizontal rectangular region with a circle inside, labeled with '2R' as its diameter. To the right of the circle, an upward vector 'qE' and a downward vector 'mg' are shown. White text below the diagrams explains the transformation: "As E₀ = 0, the transformed E = V₀ x B, where V₀ is chosen Such that it cancels mg. In this frame, Particle executes Circular motion." It then shows the derivation "So qVE = mg => qV₀B = mg => V₀ = mg / qB", with the final expression for V₀ in a green box. Another equation, "Also R = mUᵣₑₗ / qB", is at the bottom left. The stylus cursor moves between the diagrams and text, emphasizing the cycloidal motion in the ground frame transforming into circular motion in the moving frame.

At 00:27, the screen quickly transitions back to the initial derivation slide, with the stylus cursor briefly pointing at the final result. At 00:38, the screen changes again to a promotional slide titled "OTHER IMPORTANT SERIES" in yellow. Below this, four series names are listed in cyan blue: "1) PATHFINDER SOLUTIONS", "2) OLYMPIAD WORKOUT SERIES", "3) 'AITS' SELECT SERIES", and "4) "RESOLVED" SERIES". A small image on the left features "PHYSICS SIR JEE™" and "PATH FINDER SOLUTIONS SERIES" on a blue background. Yellow text at the bottom reads, "LINKS OF PLAYLISTS IN DESCRIPTION BELOW". The stylus cursor moves over these elements as the speaker concludes.
